description: Import Microsoft Fabric workspace items (Lakehouse, Warehouse, Notebook, DataPipeline, Dataflow) as Dagster assets via the Fabric REST API.

outputs.description: One Dagster asset per discovered Fabric item.

import_notebooks.description: Notebooks become materializable @assets -- materializing them runs the notebook job.
import_notebooks.label: Import Notebooks

filter_by_name_pattern.description: Regex applied to Fabric item display names for inclusion.
filter_by_name_pattern.label: Filter By Name (regex)

exclude_name_pattern.description: Regex applied to Fabric item display names for exclusion.
exclude_name_pattern.label: Exclude Name (regex)

upstream_asset_keys.description: Asset keys that all imported assets wait for (lineage-only).
upstream_asset_keys.label: Upstream Asset Keys

key.label: Key
key.description: Disambiguator for the cached discovery-state key. Without this, two FabricWorkspaceComponent instances pointed at the same workspace_id but different import_*/filter settings would share one state file.

default_parameters.label: Default Parameters
default_parameters.description: Parameters passed to every triggered Notebook/DataPipeline/Dataflow job (e.g. a load date), merged with item_parameters. A plain {name: value} dict, converted internally to Fabric's documented Parameter[] request shape.

item_parameters.label: Item Parameters
item_parameters.description: Per-item parameter overrides, keyed by the Fabric item's display name. Merged over default_parameters for that specific item.

polling_sensor.label: Polling Sensor
polling_sensor.description: If true, adds a polling sensor that detects new Fabric item job completions and emits AssetObservation events. Matches the `polling_sensor` convention on FivetranAccountComponent and SnowflakeWorkspaceComponent. Off by default -- opt in explicitly.

sensor_check_interval_seconds.label: Sensor Check Interval Seconds
sensor_check_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between polling-sensor ticks. Only used when polling_sensor=True. Distinct from workspace.poll_interval_seconds, which governs the in-asset trigger-and-wait loop for runs Dagster itself kicks off.

max_retries.label: Max Retries
max_retries.description: Max retries requested via dg.RetryRequested for a Fabric run that fails with a transient/retriable signal (Fabric's own failureReason.isRetriable, or a capacity/throttle keyword fallback when that flag is absent). Only used when the failure is classified as retriable -- a non-retriable failure (e.g. auth, bad notebook code) always fails immediately regardless of this value.

retry_backoff_seconds.label: Retry Backoff Seconds
retry_backoff_seconds.description: Base seconds to wait before a retry; doubles per attempt (exponential backoff) using the run's retry_number.

load_date_parameter.label: Load Date Parameter
load_date_parameter.description: Fabric parameter name to auto-inject with the current date (see load_date_timezone) on every triggered run, merged with default_parameters/item_parameters. Override a specific run with the 'fabric/load_date_override' run tag (e.g. for a backfill). Unset by default -- no date parameter is injected.

load_date_timezone.label: Load Date Timezone
load_date_timezone.description: IANA timezone used to compute 'today' for load_date_parameter. Only used when load_date_parameter is set.

pool.label: Pool
pool.description: Dagster concurrency pool assigned to every triggered Notebook/DataPipeline/Dataflow asset, e.g. to cap how many Fabric jobs run concurrently against a shared capacity. Overridable per item via item_pools.

item_pools.label: Item Pools
item_pools.description: Per-item concurrency pool overrides, keyed by the Fabric item's display name (same convention as item_parameters). Overrides `pool` for that specific item.

lakehouse_id.label: Lakehouse ID
lakehouse_id.description: OneLake item (GUID) to read exit_value_file from. Required when exit_value_file is set. A Notebook has no OneLake storage of its own -- notebookutils.fs resolves relative paths against its attached default Lakehouse, not the notebook item itself -- so this must name a real storage-bearing item (a Lakehouse or Warehouse), not the triggered item's own id.

exit_value_file.label: Exit Value File
exit_value_file.description: Path (relative to lakehouse_id's OneLake Files/ root, e.g. 'exit_value.txt' or 'exit_values/{load_date}.txt') to a file a Notebook writes with its own notebookutils.notebook.exit(...) value, which the Job Scheduler API itself cannot surface. Read back via OneLake's ADLS Gen2-compatible API (a separate storage.azure.com OAuth scope) after the job reports Completed. The value is attached as 'fabric/exit_value' metadata. A read failure (auth, 404, network) raises a real Failure -- fails CLOSED, since the point of this field is to catch bad data that would otherwise pass as a green materialization. See data_failure_exit_values to turn a specific value into a data-quality Failure.

data_failure_exit_values.label: Data Failure Exit Values
data_failure_exit_values.description: Exit values (read via exit_value_file) that should turn an otherwise-Completed Fabric run into a dg.Failure with failure_class='data' -- e.g. a notebook that signals 'no_rows_processed' without itself failing. Only used when exit_value_file is set.
